task: Teacher-free predictive-feature acquisition for arbitrary finite-state/HMM processes

status_key.derived_conditional: Proof is written here, but conclusion depends on stated computational hardness assumption.
status_key.primary_prior_art: Claim is directly stated or constructed in cited primary literature; its published proof was not fully re-certified.
status_key.astra_source_reported: Recovered from a pinned Astra report; not externally validated or automatically treated as proved.
status_key.open_gap: Exact missing theorem/interface implication; no solution supplied.
status_key.not_reopened: Known only from inherited mention; intentionally unused and unverified here.

claims.claim: For P_s(a,b)=2^-(d+1)[1+theta(-1)^(s·a+b)], any evaluator q with TV(P_s,q)<=theta/16 yields a clean parity predictor of uniform error <=1/8 by comparing q(a,0),q(a,1). Goldreich-Levin plus fresh LPN validation recovers s in randomized polynomial time. Therefore a uniform polynomial-time passive evaluator learner for this O(d)-state family would solve search-LPN.
claims.assumption: Standard search-LPN/noisy-parity computational hardness at a fixed eta in (0,1/2); not unconditional.

resource_accounting.training: R resets use R ordinary LPN samples; simulation costs O(Rd+O) local bits of work for O revealed symbols and O(d) source-side buffering, plus learner costs.
resource_accounting.evaluator: Polynomially many arbitrary-prefix calls; two joint point-probability evaluations per parity-predictor query. Exact comparison or joint absolute precision <=2^-d*theta/8 (d+O(log(1/theta)) fractional bits) suffices.
resource_accounting.extractor: Goldreich-Levin polynomial in d and log(1/delta) calls/work at the constant heavy-coefficient threshold.
resource_accounting.validation: O(theta^-2 log(|L|/delta)) fresh LPN examples; naive scoring O(d|L|theta^-2 log(|L|/delta)) bit operations.
resource_accounting.memory: Learner/model representation and evaluator workspace plus polynomial-in-d extractor workspace; streaming heavy-bucket variant retains O(d/theta^2) candidate-prefix bits and O(d) temporary bits.

claims.primary_source: Kearns et al., STOC 1994, Conjecture 15 and Theorem 16, PDF lines 1215-1258 (two-track noisy-parity PFA construction and evaluator classifier). The TV threshold and search extraction are the present explicit specialization, not a novelty claim.

claims.claim: If q exposes valid arbitrary-prefix next-bit conditional probabilities, g(a)=q(0|a)-q(1|a) obeys E_U|g-theta chi_s|<=4 TV(P_s,q). At TV<=theta/16, g has Fourier coefficient at s at least 3theta/4. An explicit bucket-energy/Goldreich-Levin extraction is polynomial and recovers s with fresh LPN validation.

resource_accounting.conditional_precision: O(log(1/theta)) bits for g to accuracy theta/32; if conditionals are obtained by division by a tiny prefix mass, that polynomial-time finite-bit division contract is required explicitly.
resource_accounting.extractor: The Astra N13 self-contained bucket implementation gives O(d theta^-6 log(d/(theta delta))) predictor evaluations and a list of at most 16/theta^2 masks.

claims.route_source: Astra N13 pinned page, lines 36-90, itself attributes the mechanism to classical Goldreich-Levin/Kushilevitz-Mansour and Kearns et al.; this is not new Fourier recovery.

claims.claim: Noisy parity is generated by a two-track, d-level probabilistic finite automaton. A standard edge-emitting-to-state-emitting lift yields an ordinary HMM with O(d) states; Astra N13 records at most 4d+4 for its convention-specific construction.
claims.primary_source: Kearns et al. Theorem 16 proof sketch, PDF lines 1223-1251; exact ordinary-HMM state bound is independently recorded in Astra N13 lines 24-33, not a novel property.

claims.claim: Mahajan et al. Theorem 2 learns rank-r finite-horizon laws from chosen-prefix conditional samples with a fidelity parameter. Their noisy-parity HMM has rank <=2T and fidelity theta^2/2, so the constant-noise LPN example is efficiently learnable with that stronger service. Liu-Moitra Theorem 1.3 learns arbitrary finite-rank laws from chosen-prefix conditional queries without the fidelity assumption.
claims.scope: These services let the learner choose a prefix and receive a source-conditional future sample; they are not passive whole-trajectory samples and are not the A06 misspecified-teacher interface.
claims.source_ranges: Mahajan et al., Theorem 2 PDF p.4 and p.39 lines 2665-69; Proposition 17 p.24 lines 1318-69. Liu-Moitra Definitions 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 lines 92-102.

claims.claim: Given passive P trajectories and exact chosen-prefix teacher-Q probabilities/simulation with KL(P||Q)<=zeta, A06 reports a stopped-prefix Hellinger control, rank-doubling bounded-task table compression with source-task MSE <=(2pi+2)zeta plus sampling/SDP error, and finite-prefix future-column acquisition.
claims.scope: The report labels itself partial and not externally validated. The static construction's proof and computational diagnostics were not independently replayed in this child task.
claims.source_ranges: Pinned A06 page lines 18-31 (interface), 82-125 (Hellinger), 126-216 (static compression), 217-265 (finite-prefix acquisition).

claims.claim: The finite-prefix static SDP does not yield an evaluable feature map for fresh prefixes, an update from compact state plus next symbol, stable inter-cut basis maps, or accumulated finite-precision control. Acquiring such maps with actual-path loss O(zeta)+epsilon^2 and no r/H multiplier is the missing service.
claims.scope: This is a precise unresolved implication in the A06 route, not a proven impossibility. Passive LPN hardness does not transfer automatically because A06 gives Q evaluation/simulation during acquisition.
claims.source_ranges: Pinned A06 page lines 266-295; interface at lines 18-31.

claims.claim: Astra N25 reports a four-state paired-bit P and positive low-KL teacher Q with an off-source parity-logit rule; independent prefix/suffix splices create a constant-mass Walsh rectangle of rank 2^(k-1). This refutes inferring uniform splice-logit low rank from actual-path KL alone.
claims.scope: Only the proposed uniform-splice transfer is falsified. No universal teacher-assisted learner is ruled out; diagnostics were not independently rerun here.

claims.claim: Hsu-Kakade-Zhang's passive spectral method assumes positive initial mass and full-rank transition/emission matrices; their bounds depend on inverse singular values. Their Theorem 7's conditional-probability guarantee adds positive stochasticity alpha and nondegeneracy gamma parameters with explicit inverse-power costs.
claims.scope: This is a positive structured subclass, not arbitrary rank-deficient/no-margin HMM acquisition.

claims.claim: Predictive-state representations already encode states as predictions of future observable tests and update normalized linear predictions; spectral/HSE methods estimate such coordinates from moments under chosen-test/basis and conditioning assumptions. Generic latent-parameter identifiability is not itself a finite-sample stable acquisition or recurrence theorem.
claims.scope: Feature-map language or latent-state identification cannot be counted as an acquired fresh-prefix feature service without the relevant basis, data, and update costs.

claims.claim: No inherited prior-workspace rare-prefix result is relied on in this report. It remains unverified in this task.
